---
title: "Demos"
subtitle: "Cards and assertions at work in the browser"
---

Each demo reads published stores from the [gallery](index.qmd) straight from
their bucket and draws them in the page, to show one thing a card records
and what goes wrong for a reader that ignores it.

[Five costumes, one grid](demo/costumes.html): five published Zarr stores
hold the same sea ice on the same polar stereographic grid, each declaring it
differently: CF with 1-D axes, CF with a renamed grid mapping, a transform
with an EPSG code and a pyramid, a transform with PROJJSON only, and nothing
but 2-D longitude and latitude. Four common reader rules each place a
different subset. The card reads every declaration, checks they agree, and
places the first four, which then draw identically cell for cell.

[One assertion, end to end](demo/index.html): two published Zarr stores hold
the same Antarctic sea ice. One declares its grid in six numbers and a CRS;
the other hides the same grid behind 68 MB of 2-D longitude and latitude, so
a reader that wants a declared grid refuses it. The page applies a published
assertion of 2 KB to the second store, in the browser, and checks that it
then draws identically to the first: every value, the transform, the CRS and
every pixel.

[An honest refusal](demo/tripolar.html): an ocean model's tripolar grid,
published with 1-D axes that are exact south of 65 N and wrong north of it,
beside its true 2-D positions. The page shows where the axes go wrong, and
why a grid fit refuses to assert a frame: no six numbers describe this grid.

[The numbers are not the values](demo/packing.html): sea surface temperature
stored as 16-bit integers in hundredths of a degree. Skipping CF packing puts
most of the ocean past the top of the colour ramp; applying the packing the
card reads from metadata gives values equal, bit for bit in float32, to a
twin stored as float32.

[Which cells are missing?](demo/fill.html): three published stores under
four reader rules for fill values. STAC `nodata` alone misses a store that
declares none, and misses -1e20 against float32 cells; a CF `_FillValue`
parsed as a number misses xarray's base64 encoding. The card reads every
source, casts each to the stored type, and masks every fill cell in all
three.
